# Stellar validation: flares, pulsations and CHEOPS

Protocol v3 (`docs/results/stellar_validation_protocol_v3.json`, sha256 `c978f04c24b831c7f09d6ddd4d84e94cdee9b297a9ee87358ad8614da8f1b1ba`, committed in `b2ac54c26149`), frozen 2026-10-22, seed 20261022; stellar code fingerprint `1d625f69621398a4…` (each item records the fingerprint of the files it depends on, this script included). Generated 2026-10-22T06:54:39+00:00.

**How far to trust this.** Protocol v1 (frozen 2026-10-21) was not a blind protocol: its thresholds, and the algorithms it tested, were revised during development while looking at these same targets. v2 (committed 2f347d1) was committed before its run. v3 follows the review of the v2 results: it is committed on its own, before any v3 result exists, and its results record this file's sha256 and the commit that added it. v3 still uses the targets v1 and v2 used, so it is a re-test after review fixes, not an independent validation. Two criteria were relaxed after v1 and one tightened after v2; each check says so.

Changes from v2:

- Injection placement (all injection items): amplitude and FWHM are drawn once per injection and only the position is redrawn (up to 200 tries; an injection with no valid position is counted as unplaced, with its FWHM). A position is valid when the flare's start (one FWHM before the peak) and its peak plus three FWHM fall inside one stretch of data (cf. Poyatos et al. 2025, Sect. 2.3: only flares whose start and stop fall within one visit); the wider span (two FWHM before to eight after) must still not overlap another injection or a real flare. v2 redrew the FWHM with every position and required the whole wider span inside a stretch, so 60% of the CHEOPS injections had FWHM 0.5-1 min against 23% expected. The CHEOPS item reports the placed-FWHM histogram next to the injection gate.
- Merge check (new, reported, not counted): two-component flares (second peak 5-50% of the first, log-uniform; 1-5 FWHM later) injected on Proxima and GJ 1243, the stars that did not tune the shape test; the merged fraction is reported overall and by ratio and separation. A secondary below min_component_fraction = 0.1 of the primary cannot be kept as a component by construction. No pass criterion: there is no published reference rate.
- False-split check: the 15% limit applies to the Wilson 95% upper bound of the pooled Proxima + GJ 1243 rate, like the other checks' interval bounds (v2 used the point estimate). Proxima is reported on its own as well as pooled.
- Proxima energies: Medina et al.'s TESS-band luminosity implied by their Table 3 (Energy / ED) is reported next to ours, with each input (TESS magnitude, distance, zero point) swapped in turn, Medina et al.'s values read from their Table 1. The proxima_band_energy check is unchanged and still uses TIC inputs. A luminosity-matched cross-check (our data ED times L from their TESS magnitude) is reported, labelled, and not counted.
- Status rule: a capability is validated when every counted check passes, partly validated when more than half pass, and otherwise not validated, always shown with the count (k of n checks pass). v2 called any capability with one passing check partly validated.
- CHEOPS-derived results (cheops_flares, hr10_cheops, cheops_pycheops and the CHEOPS part of denoise_grid) are written to docs/results/stellar_validation_cheops.json and .md under ESA's CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO terms; the main files keep only the CHEOPS capability's status and the pass or fail of its checks.
- Each item's code fingerprint now covers scripts/stellar_validation.py as well as the modules it uses, so a change to how an item is measured invalidates its cached result.
- Checks relaxed after v1 (proxima_bright_recall, pycheops_same_input) and tightened after v2 (false_split) are marked in their text.

Changes from v1 (in v2):

- Flare energies: the TESS magnitude route uses Sullivan et al. (2015)'s band-integrated zero point (4.03e-6 erg s^-1 cm^-2), as Medina et al. (2020) do, and is the primary band luminosity; the Teff and radius route is reported beside it. TESS items use TIC values only (no Teff fallback); CHEOPS items may use the CHEOPS archive's Teff, labelled.
- Flare morphology: the BIC uses an effective number of points for the noise's lag-one correlation, and an extra component must be a visible peak (3 sigma and a tenth of the strongest component). A false-split check is added.
- Flux-inverted null: the real flares' windows are masked first.
- Injections: placed wholly inside one stretch of data, kept clear of real flares' full extent; blends (recovered ED more than 1.5 x injected) are excluded from the false-split rate and counted.
- CHEOPS flare comparisons with Poyatos et al. (2025, journal version: 349 flares, ~40% complex, +34% from denoising, alpha 1.92 +/- 0.07) count under the CHEOPS capability, and only when the CHEOPS null and injection checks pass; otherwise they are inconclusive.
- Proxima recall of bright flares: the published-ED >= 3 s bins are pooled (v1 required each bin, one of which held 4 flares).
- pycheops same-input check: passes on a visit when our decorrelation matches pycheops' to < 10 ppm rms, or reaches a lower rms on the same points and terms (the least-squares optimum is unique; v1 failed a visit on which pycheops' fit is off it).
- Pulsations: combination flags use the ten strongest frequencies as parents and a quarter-Rayleigh (or 3 sigma) tolerance, and a chance rate is reported; added checks on that rate, on TOI-197's delta-nu to 1 microHz, and on HR 10's granulation frequency with Salmon et al.'s averaged-periodogram estimator.

CHEOPS-derived numbers are not in this file: they are in `stellar_validation_cheops.json` and `stellar_validation_cheops.md`, under ESA's CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO terms (see LICENSING.md). This file keeps only the CHEOPS capability's status and the pass or fail of its checks.

Every comparison is against **published numbers**; where ours and theirs disagree, both are shown. Flares and frequencies are *detected* at the significance stated; nothing here is a confirmation, and types are heuristic.

| Flux-inverted null | 0 | |

Our default ED is the integral of the fitted template, which keeps the slow tail below the noise; Medina et al. sum the data over the flare (their §3.3), so the like-for-like energy uses our data-summed ED. Medina et al. derive the TESS-band luminosity from the TESS magnitude, the distance and Sullivan et al. (2015)'s zero point (4.03 × 10⁻⁶ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻²), as SetuHQ's magnitude route now does: L_TESS = 9.29e+29 erg/s (TIC Tmag 7.36, 1.301 pc). TIC v8.2 has no Teff for Proxima Cen, so the Teff and radius route is unavailable here.

**Why the energies differ: the TESS magnitude.** Medina et al.'s table implies L_TESS = Energy / ED = 8.21e+29 erg/s (median of 134 flares; 5-95%: 8e+29-8.4e+29); ours is 9.29e+29 erg/s, a ratio of 1.131. Swapping one input at a time (their Table 1: Tmag 7.49, 1.30 pc; TIC: Tmag 7.36, 1.30119 pc; zero point Sullivan et al. (2015), 4.03e-6 erg s^-1 cm^-2: the same):

| Inputs | L_TESS (erg/s) | / Medina et al.'s implied L |
|---|---|---|
| ours (TIC Tmag, TIC distance) | 9.287e+29 | 1.131 |
| Medina et al.'s Tmag, TIC distance | 8.239e+29 | 1.003 |
| TIC Tmag, Medina et al.'s distance | 9.27e+29 | 1.129 |
| Medina et al.'s Tmag and distance | 8.224e+29 | 1.002 |

The TESS magnitude accounts for the difference (TIC v8.2 gives 7.36, Medina et al. 7.49); the distance changes L by 0.2% and the zero point is the same. The protocol check above (proxima_band_energy) is kept as run, with our TIC inputs, and fails as recorded.

*Luminosity-matched cross-check (not a protocol check; not counted):* the same data ED times L_TESS from Medina et al.'s Tmag (8.24e+29 erg/s), ours / published: 1.18 [1.02, 1.34] (n = 53). What remains is the difference between our data-summed ED and theirs.

Like with like, on the tuning star: before the review fixes (no effective-N correction, no visibility rule) single flares on AU Mic came back split 41% of the time (21 of 51, blends included; the AR(1) correction alone gave 39%); after them, 6/71 = 0.08. Both are AU Mic, the star the rule was tuned on, so neither is a validation number.

### Merges: two-component flares that come back as one

A second Mendoza peak at 5-50% of the first (log-uniform), 1-5 FWHM later, injected on stars that did not tune the shape test. An extra component must reach 0.1 of the strongest one (and 3σ), so **a secondary below 10% of the primary cannot be kept by construction**; those are the first ratio bin. Merged = the detected flare holding the first peak also holds the second and has one component; detected flares that also hold another injection's peak are blends and left out. Reported; the protocol sets no pass criterion (no published reference rate).

### HR 10, TESS sectors 2 and 29, against Salmon et al. 2024

| Sector | Ours (S/N ≥ 4) | Ours (S/N ≥ 5) | Published (S/N ≥ 5) | Recall 3σ | Recall 1/T [95% CI] | Top-10 recall 3σ / 1/T | Amplitude ours / published |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 63 | 51 | 41 | 0.93 | 0.95 [0.84, 0.99] | 1.00 / 1.00 | 1.09 [1.07, 1.10] (n = 39) |
| 29 | 52 | 42 | 62 | 0.74 | 0.74 [0.62, 0.83] | 1.00 / 1.00 | 1.01 [0.99, 1.03] (n = 46) |

Granulation-like background (S29): our Harvey characteristic frequencies 58 µHz (exponents 2.7); with Salmon et al.'s estimator (one-day periodograms averaged, one Harvey profile): 69.9189 µHz; Salmon et al.: b = 150.87 µHz. Salmon et al. fit one Harvey component to an averaged periodogram (25 one-day series); SetuHQ's default fits one or two to the full periodogram by maximum likelihood, and the validation also applies their estimator. A mismatch here is reported as one (check hr10_granulation), not explained away.
- S2: 12 of the S/N ≥ 4 frequencies flagged as possible combinations; a random frequency would be flagged with probability 0.018 (tolerance 0.00912 d⁻¹, 10 parents), about 0.95 chance flags expected.
- S29: 11 of the S/N ≥ 4 frequencies flagged as possible combinations; a random frequency would be flagged with probability 0.028 (tolerance 0.010 d⁻¹, 10 parents), about 1.18 chance flags expected.
- Null, ar1 surrogates of the S29 residual: 0.60 false frequencies per light curve on average, 40% of 10 surrogates with any.
- Null, background surrogates of the S29 residual: 0.30 false frequencies per light curve on average, 30% of 10 surrogates with any.
- Type: hybrid δ Scuti/γ Doradus (low confidence): 37 independent frequencies at ≥ 5 d⁻¹ (75% of the amplitude), 4 below; Teff 8840 K is outside the δ Scuti/γ Doradus range (6300-8800 K).

### TOI-197, TESS sector 2, solar-like oscillations, against Huber et al. 2019

| Quantity | SetuHQ (bootstrap 1σ) | Huber et al. 2019 | z |
|---|---|---|---|
| numax (µHz) | 433.2 ± 6.186 | 430.0 ± 18.0 | 0.17 |
| Δν (µHz) | 28.7958 ± 2.378 | 28.94 ± 0.15 | -0.06 |

SetuHQ reads SPOC PDCSAP; Huber et al. used a TASOC light curve. Envelope ΔBIC 19.2. The Δν search window is 0.7-1.4 × the scaling value (28.544 µHz), about ±6 µHz around the published value, so the tighter check asks for agreement within 1 µHz; our bootstrap uncertainty is large because the bootstrap redraws a smoothed spectrum.

## CHEOPS

Status: **not validated (2 of 5 checks pass)**, 2 inconclusive (gated). The CHEOPS results (flares against Poyatos et al. 2025 with their gates and the placed-FWHM histogram, the CHEOPS denoising grid, HR 10 on CHEOPS and the pycheops comparison) are in `stellar_validation_cheops.md` and `.json`, under ESA's CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO terms, with ESA's acknowledgement, the programme and visit IDs, the credit lines and the citations.

## What is not validated

- Flare energies: on TESS they use the TESS magnitude and distance (Sullivan et al. 2015 zero point) when the TIC has them, else TIC Teff and radius; on CHEOPS (no magnitude route) the TIC radius and, where the TIC has no Teff, the Teff from the CHEOPS archive, labelled. A star with neither route gets energies reported as unavailable.
- AU Mic sector 1 is the tuning star of the flare shape test: its numbers are reported, its null is not counted.
- GJ 1243: no machine-readable per-flare TESS catalogue was found; detections are reported, not compared.
- GJ 65: no per-flare table is public for Bruno et al. (2024); only an internal 120 s vs 20 s check.
- Poyatos et al. (2025) worked on 3-s CHEOPS imagettes reduced with PIPE; DACE serves DRP subarray light curves (about 42 s and longer), so the CHEOPS comparison is of aggregate numbers on different data products, not flare by flare, and it counts only when the CHEOPS null and injection gates pass. Their per-flare catalogue is not public.
- Bruno et al. (2024): no per-flare catalogue; their complex fraction (≳ 30%) is quoted for context only.
- Wavelet denoising: tuned and checked by injection on SetuHQ's own data; Poyatos et al.'s optimal parameters were found on imagettes and are not reproduced here.
- HR 10 CHEOPS frequencies: Salmon et al. (2024) publish no CHEOPS frequency list; only the TESS lists are compared.
